dedupe_keys.name: array of things chicago urban sensor network data 2016 to 2021

description: Array of Things (AoT) was an experimental urban measurement network in Chicago, funded by the U.S. National Science Foundation, of modular nodes mounted about 24 to 28 feet above street intersections and built on Argonne's open-source Waggle platform; by late 2019 about 130 nodes were operating. Nodes measured air quality gases and particles, temperature, humidity, pressure, light and ultraviolet, sound level, vibration and magnetic field, with cameras used on the node for street conditions and traffic, and the project published measurements as open data, to a download site daily and to an API every five minutes. The original nodes were retired in September 2021 and the work continues through SAGE, a software-defined sensor network, and the Eclipse air quality project on Chicago bus shelters. Coverage: Chicago, 2016 to 2021. Access: historical downloads only; the linked download host could not be reached here. Licence: published as open data; the policies page was not read. Caveats: the network is retired and sensor models changed between node generations. Simulation uses: street-level environmental time series for urban heat, air quality and digital twin studies. Related records: the Newcastle Urban Observatory.
